paragraphs: The red right-turn arrow is lit. It prohibits the right turn, even though the round green lets straight-ahead and left-turning traffic go.
Wait behind the stop line. A clear gap in the oncoming traffic changes nothing while the red arrow is lit.

sourceRefs.quote: the illuminated red arrow light shall be taken as prohibiting vehicles from proceeding beyond the stop line or broken lines on the road in that direction

sourceRefs.section: Examples, circular green with red right arrow
sourceRefs.quote: Means “GO” for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.

paragraphs: How far away the oncoming car is does not matter. The handbook is explicit: do not turn right on a red arrow even when there is no traffic from the opposite direction.

sourceRefs.quote: Do not turn right even when there is no traffic from the opposite direction

paragraphs: A round green does not override an arrow. Where an arrow is lit for a movement, the arrow decides that movement; the round green only covers the movements no arrow speaks for.
Here the round green covers straight ahead and left. The red arrow covers right, so the right turn must wait.

sourceRefs.quote: turn left or right subject to any sign prohibiting left or right turn or in conjunction with the arrow light signals
Means “GO” for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.

paragraphs: An amber arrow means get ready to STOP in the direction it points. It is never a signal that the turn is about to be allowed.
Only a green arrow, or a round green with no arrow lit for your direction, lets the right turn go.

sourceRefs.quote: Means “READY TO STOP” behind the stop-line in the direction indicated.

paragraphs: The round green is lit and no arrow is lit for straight ahead. So the round green decides your movement: you may go straight when it is safe.
The red arrow is lit only for the right turn. It does not stop vehicles going straight or turning left.

sourceRefs.quote: Means “GO” for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.
Look to the right and left to ensure it is safe before you proceed.

paragraphs: A red arrow prohibits proceeding in the direction it points, and only that direction. It is not a round red.
With the round green lit, straight-ahead vehicles go; only right-turning vehicles wait.

sourceRefs.quote: the illuminated red arrow light shall be taken as prohibiting vehicles from proceeding beyond the stop line or broken lines on the road in that direction
Means “GO” for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.

paragraphs: Your straight-ahead path does not cross the oncoming car's straight-ahead path, so there is nothing to give way to. Look right and left, then go.
Waiting for oncoming traffic is a right-turn habit; it belongs to the comparison where the right arrow is not lit and the round green governs the turn.

sourceRefs.quote: Look to the right and left to ensure it is safe before you proceed.

paragraphs: Only a lit round red stops every movement on the approach. The comparison scene shows this junction with the round red lit: then even straight-ahead vehicles wait behind the stop line.
In the actual scene the round red is dark; a red arrow does not act as a round red.

sourceRefs.quote: Means “STOP”.
the illuminated red light shall be taken as prohibiting vehicles from proceeding beyond the stop line or broken lines on the road provided in conjunction with the signals

paragraphs: When no arrow is lit for the right turn, the round green governs it: you may turn right after giving way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, subject to any sign.

sourceRefs.quote: turn left or right subject to any sign prohibiting left or right turn or in conjunction with the arrow light signals

paragraphs: A green right arrow means GO in that direction after making sure oncoming traffic is clear.

sourceRefs.quote: Means “GO” but only in the direction indicated after ensuring that oncoming traffic is clear.

questions.stem: You are driving the car and want to turn right. On the signal ahead the round green light is lit and the red right-turn arrow is lit. The oncoming car is still far away, leaving a clear gap. May you turn right now?

options.text: No. Stop behind the stop line: the red arrow forbids the right turn even when the way is clear.
Yes, because the round green light is lit and the oncoming car is far enough away for a safe turn.
Yes, because the round green light is lit and green means go for every movement.
Yes, but only once the arrow turns amber, because an amber arrow means the turn is about to be allowed.

sourceRefs.quote: Do not turn right even when there is no traffic from the opposite direction

questions.stem: You are driving the car and want to go straight ahead. On the signal ahead the round green light is lit and the red right-turn arrow is lit. What may you do?

options.text: Go straight ahead when it is safe: the round green covers your movement, and the red arrow applies only to turning right.
Stop behind the stop line: a lit red arrow means every vehicle on this approach must stop.
Wait until the oncoming car has passed: on a round green, going straight must give way to oncoming traffic.
Treat it like a round red light: whenever any red lens is lit, nobody may pass the stop line.
